content: This medication should only be used when it is clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Due to the potential risk to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as colonoscopy, fecal occult blood testing, lipase/amylase levels, and liver function tests, should be performed before starting this medication and periodically during its use. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Teduglutide is used by patients with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who require intravenous (IV) nutrition and fluids. It may help reduce the amount of IV nutrition needed. Teduglutide is similar to a natural hormone in the body called GLP-2. Before using teduglutide, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Consult your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use this medication. Inject this medication under the skin as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The injection is typically administered in the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm. Do not shake the vial. Inspect the product for particles or discoloration before use; do not use the liquid if either is present. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose. Rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. To reduce bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administration. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Possible side effects include decreased appetite, difficulty sleeping, cough, flu-like symptoms, or pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. This medication may increase the risk of cancer, and your doctor will monitor you closely with laboratory and medical tests. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using teduglutide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Due to the potential risk to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication.
